title: Security & Compliance Integrated Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Compliance Evidence, Risk & Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This integrated playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s core security and compliance controls across: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, Secure SDLC controls, incident response for security incidents, evidence collection workflows for audits, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended for security engineers, platform engineers, product owners, and compliance reviewers.

Goals
- Provide a single reference for operationalizing security controls required by enterprise customers and auditors.
- Define owners, SLOs, thresholds, and procedures to ensure repeatable evidence collection.
- Describe the risk & exceptions flow for pragmatic, auditable decisions.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control plane components, and supported Private deployment packaging when the control is implemented by Redwood. Customer-managed controls are noted where applicable.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Summary:
Role-based access control is implemented across three layers: Console (UI), Control Plane APIs, and Infrastructure (cloud accounts/KMS). We use centralized identity via SSO (OIDC/SAML) backed by customer-managed identity providers for enterprise customers and Okta for Redwood corporate accounts.

Key roles and responsibilities:
- Security (owner): defines role definitions and audit policies.
- Eng Platform (operator): configures IAM role-to-service mappings and maintains automation.
- Customer Success: validates role mappings during onboarding for Dedicated/Private customers.

Canonical roles (examples):
- org:admin — full org-level admin (create/delete projects, billing)
- org:viewer — read-only org visibility
- service:deploy — deploy and rollout models/services
- service:ops — runbooks, incident actions, log access (no billing)
- developer — create API keys, access sandboxes

Authorization policies and enforcement:
- All API requests must be authenticated and authorized via the gateway policy engine (Open Policy Agent).
- Principle of least privilege by default; new roles are scoped to minimal permissions and require approval for escalation.
- Machine identities (service accounts) are scoped to single-service or single-cluster access tokens with short rotation (7 days) and automated rotation via our secrets manager.

Onboarding and approval steps (numbered):
1. Request role via Internal Access Request form (link on team wiki) with justification and owner.
2. Security reviews request within 3 business days.
3. If approved, Eng Platform updates OPA policies and creates a ticket for automation.

RBAC SLOs and metrics:
- Access request turnaround: 72 hours (target)
- Quarterly role entitlement review conducted by Security and Eng Platform

2) Audit Logging

Summary:
Audit logging captures administrative actions, access to customer data, model deployments, configuration changes, and credential operations. Logs are immutable, timestamped (UTC), and cryptographically signed for Hosted services.

Retention and storage:
- Operational logs (metrics, infra): 90 days hot storage, 365 days cold storage
- Audit logs (admin actions, access grants, key operations): 7 years (per enterprise customer contracts), default 2 years for corporate internal logs
- Customer requestable retention for Dedicated/Private documented in customer contract and automated in Private packaging.

Log schema (essential fields):
- timestamp_utc
- actor_id (SSO user / service account)
- actor_role
- action (string: e.g., grant_role, create_api_key, deploy_model)
- resource_type (project, model, key, dataset)
- resource_id
- outcome (success|failure)
- request_id (correlation id)
- src_ip

Example audit query (Kusto/SQL-like):
SELECT timestamp_utc, actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome
FROM audit_logs
WHERE resource_type = 'key' AND action = 'create_api_key' AND timestamp_utc >= '2027-04-01'
ORDER BY timestamp_utc DESC

Audit access and tooling:
- Audit logs are available to security and SRE by default; customer-accessible audit exports are available via the Console for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Export tooling supports CSV, Parquet, and secure S3 delivery with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS).

3) Data Residency & Retention

Residency principles:
- Data at rest is stored in the region selected for the workload. Hosted customers select regional endpoints.
- Customer data stored in Dedicated or Private deployments remains in customer-controlled regions and accounts where requested.
- Cross-region replication only occurs when explicitly enabled and documented in the contract.

Retention policy table:
| Data type | Default retention | Purpose | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------|---------|-------|
| Customer inputs & outputs | 30 days | Billing, support debugging | Can be extended by contract; opt-out for ephemeral workloads |
| Embeddings & model artifacts | 365 days | Reuse and caching | Sensitive datasets may require shorter retention |
| Audit logs (customer) | 7 years | Compliance | Configurable per customer |
| Metrics & monitoring | 90 days hot / 365 days cold | Capacity planning | Aggregated metrics retained longer |

Retention procedures (numbered):
1. Data owners classify data during model onboarding (see model-onboarding guide).
2. Retention settings are applied at the storage bucket level with lifecycle policies.
3. Deletion requests: Security reviews deletion requests and issues a deletion ticket; automation runs and returns provenance record.

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle)

Principles:
- Shift-left security: dependency scanning, SCA, static analysis, and secrets detection integrated into CI/CD.
- Mandatory code review, testing, and canary deploys for production-impacting changes.
- Threat modeling and design review required for services storing customer data or performing cryptographic operations.

Required controls in CI/CD:
- SAST run on PRs; results must be triaged before merge (severity >= high must be fixed).
- Dependency scanning (automated) with weekly SBOM updates.
- Container image signing and provenance recorded.
- Infrastructure-as-code templates go through policy-as-code validation (terraform fmt, tflint, Conftest/OPA).

Release checklist (numbered):
1. PR approval by at least one maintainer and one security reviewer for sensitive changes.
2. Successful CI pipeline including unit, integration, and security checks.
3. Canary deployment to staging; 24-hour health monitoring.
4. Gradual rollout and automated rollback on error budget breach.

5) Incident Response: Security Incidents and Playbooks

Incident classification:
- Sev1: Active data exfiltration or production outage affecting multiple customers
- Sev2: Privilege escalation or lateral movement detected in internal systems
- Sev3: Single-customer impact or contained configuration error

High-level incident actions (numbered):
1. Triage: On-call SRE + Security acknowledge within 15 minutes for Sev1/Sev2, 1 hour for Sev3.
2. Containment: Isolate affected services, rotate credentials, and apply WAF/firewall rules as needed.
3. Investigation: Collect immutable snapshots (audit log slice, DB snapshots, network captures).
4. Notification: Notify impacted customers per contract SLAs; escalate to Legal/PR for Sev1.
5. Remediation & Recovery: Apply fixes, restore services, run verification tests.
6. Postmortem: Publish a blameless postmortem within 7 business days for Sev1/Sev2 and 14 days for Sev3.

Evidence collection steps (for investigation):
- Preserve audit log slice (query range before/after event) and export as signed Parquet.
- Collect container runtime metadata and image checksum.
- Capture host forensic snapshot (if applicable) and record chain-of-custody.

CLI example to collect audit slice (internal tooling):
redwood-audit export --from 2027-05-01T00:00:00Z --to 2027-05-01T02:00:00Z --filter "action in (\"access_data\", \"create_api_key\")" --output s3://redwood-incident-evidence/INC-1234/

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Control owners and evidence types:
- RBAC: periodic entitlement reviews, policy artifacts, sample access logs (CSV)
- Audit logging: signed audit archives, retention config, access policy
- Data residency: region config screenshots, storage bucket policies, contract clauses
- SDLC: build logs, SAST reports, release checklist artifacts

Evidence collection playbook (numbered):
1. Security receives auditor request with controls in scope.
2. Security identifies owners and starts evidence collection ticket.
3. Use automation to generate artifact bundle (signed, time-stamped).
4. Review bundle with control owner; redact customer-identifying fields unless requested.
5. Deliver via secure file share (SFTP/S3 with pre-signed URL) and track delivery.

Retention and attestation:
- Evidence bundles are retained for 7 years where required by contract.
- Security maintains an evidence index with manifest files and hash checksums.

7) Risk & Exceptions Process

When deviations from standard controls are requested (e.g., extended retention, cross-region replication, role scope exceptions), the following process applies:
1. Submit Exception Request (form + business justification).
2. Security performs risk assessment (likelihood & impact) and documents compensating controls.
3. For high-risk exceptions, CISO approval required and Legal review.
4. Approved exceptions are time-limited (max 12 months) with required monitoring and quarterly review.
5. Exceptions are logged in the risk register with owner, mitigations, and expiration date.

Decision matrix (summary):
- Low risk: Security approves; quarterly review.
- Medium risk: Security + Product approves; mitigation plan required.
- High risk: CISO+Legal approval, explicit customer-aware consent if customer data impacted.

Appendices
A. Ownership table
- Security: policy, audits, exception approvals
- Eng Platform: RBAC automation, policy deployment
- Eng SRE: logging infrastructure, incident triage
- Product: customer-facing retention options and contract clauses

B. Useful commands & queries
- Rotate service account: redwood-secrets rotate --service account-name --force
- Export audit logs: redwood-audit export --from <ts> --to <ts> --output <s3-path>
- Validate terraform: terraform validate && tflint && conftest test --policy=policy/

C. Contacts & escalation
- Security Pager: sec-oncall@redwood.example.com (Sev1 coverage)
- Eng SRE Pager: sre-oncall@redwood.example.com
- CISO (approval): ciso@redwood.example.com
